full_judgment:
2. The petitioners as plaintiffs instituted S.C.C. Suit No.7 of 1997 in the court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Chittagong exercising S.C.C. Jurisdiction impleading the opposite parties being the defendants praying for eviction of the monthly tenants and for realisation of arrear rents and compensation alleging, inter alia, that the plaintiffs are the owners of the shop premises by inheritance and one Dulal Chandra Das and Sunil Chandra Das, the predecessors of the opposite party was inducted as temporary monthly ejectable tenants at a monthly rent of Tk. 500/- and a deed of agreement was executed between the parties on 15.1.1986 and that the tenants paid rents regularly up to the months of November, 1996 and did not pay any rent since December, 1996 and became a defaulter. The plaintiffs served a notice dated 5.3.97 under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act terminating the tenancy on the expiry of 31.3.97 but without any result and hence the suit. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing a written statement contending that their predecessors Dulal Chandra Das and Sunil Chandra Das were running a business of sweetmeet shop as monthly tenants on the basis of a deed of agreement for 5(five) years executed between the parties on 1.1.1980 and that the defendants paid the monthly rents up to the month of November, 1996 and paid the rent for the month of December on 5.1.97 but the plaintiff No. did not grant any receipt assuring the defendant that he would grant receipt on acceptance of rents for the month of January, 1997 and. accordingly the defendant paid the rent for the month of January, 1997 on 4.2.97 and asked for receipt for 2 months when again plaintiff assured the defendants that he would grant receipt on receipt for the rent for the next month. The defendant tendered the rent for the month of February. 1997 on 1.3.97 and demanded rent receipts for the months of December, 1996 and January, 1997 when the plaintiff refused to accept the rent for the month of February. The defendant then sent the rent for the month of January by money order on 2.197 which was refused by the plaintiff. No. 1 and the money order returned to the defendant No. 1 who then tiled H.R.C. Case No. 34 of 1997 in the house rent controller and has been depositing the monthly rent according to law and they did not become defaulter in respect of the suit premises. The defendant further alleged that the plaintiff does not bonafide require the suit premises as he has three other shops to the adjacent of the suit premises and that notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was not served on the defendants. The defendants accordingly prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 4. The learned S.C.C. Judge, framed necessary issues and on consideration of the evidence on record came to the finding that admittedly the plaintiffs are the owners of the Shop premises and the defendants predecessors Dulal Chandra Das and Sunil Chandra Das were tenants under the plaintiffs on the basis of a deed of agreement Ext. 1. The trial court further found that- Dulal Chandra Das, the predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-4 paid monthly rent regularly up to the month of November, 1996. The learned S.C.C. Judge then placed onus on the plaintiff to prove payment of rent by the defendant for the months of December and January and on consideration of the evidence on record came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs could not prove non-payment of rent by the defendants for the months of December. 1996 and January, 1997. The trial court then considered the evidence of D. Ws. 1 and 2 and came to the finding that these two witnesses proved payment of rent by the defendants to the plaintiff for the months of December, 1996 and January, 1997. The learned S.C.C. Judge then found that the defendant tendered the rent for the month of February, 1997 but the plaintiffs refused to receive the some and accordingly the defendants sent the rent for the month of February 1997 to the plaintiff by money order but the money order was not received by the plaintiffs and the same was returned to the defendants then started depositing the rents in H.R.C. Case No. 34 of 1997 and that they are depositing rents regularly in the said rent deposited case. The trial court accordingly came to the finding that the defendants are holding over the suit premises and that they are not defaulters in payment of monthly rents. The learned S.C.C. Judge on consideration of the evidence recorded a finding "সুতরাং সাক্ষ্য প্রমানে ইহা স্পষ্ট প্রমানিত যে, বিবাদীদের পূর্ববর্তী মারা যাওয়ার পর ১নং বাদীর কাছে ডিসেম্বর/৯৬ ও জানুয়ারী/৯৭ ইং মাসের ভাড়া যথারীতি আদায় দেয়া সত্বেও বাদীপক্ষ বিবাদীগণকে ভাড়ার রশিদ প্রদান করে নাই।" The learned Judge on consideration of the evidence came to the finding " সাক্ষ্য প্রমানে ইহা স্পষ্ট প্রমানিত যে, বাদীগণ বিবাদীদের নালিশী দোকানে ব্যবসার উন্নতি দেখে প্রতিহিংসা পরায়ন হয়ে উদ্দেশ্য প্রনোদিত ভাবে বিবাদীগনকে ভাড়া খেলাপী বানানোর জন্য ডিসেম্বর/৯৬ ও জানুয়ারী/৯৭ ইং মাসের ভাড়া গ্রহন করা সত্তেও ভাড়ার রশিদ না দিয়ে পরবর্তীতে ফেব্রুয়ারী /৯৭ ইং মাসের ভাড়া ইচ্ছাকৃত ভাবে গ্রহন না করে বিবাদীগণকে নালিশী দোকান থেকে বে-আইনী ভাবে উচ্ছেদ করার মানসে মিথ্যা মোকদ্দমা আনয়ন করেছে। নালিশী দোকানে বিবাদীগণ Holding over ক্রমে ভাড়াটিয়া স্বত্বে আইনানুগভাবে দখলকার আছে এবং বিবাদীগণ ভাড়া খেলাপী নয় ও হওয়ার কোন কারণ নেই।”  The trial court then found that the plaintiff does not bonafide require the suit premises and the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was duly served. Accordingly by judgment and decree dated 14.9.99 the learned S.C.C. Judge dismissed the suit. 

 6. Mr. Rabi Shankar Chakraborty, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners has taken me through the impugned judgment of the court below and submits the court below committed a serious error of law on, placing the onus on the plaintiffs to prove non-payment of monthly rents by the defendants to the plaintiff and thereby failed to prove that the defendants are defaulters in respect of the suit premises. According to the learned Advocate, section 13 of the Premises Rent Control Act provides that every tenant, who makes a payment on account of rent of any premises to his landlord, shall be entitled to obtain forthwith from the landlord a written receipt for the amount paid by him signed by the landlord and the Lord shalt grant a written receipt for the amount paid by the tenant singed by the landlord. It therefore appears that the tenant is- the custodian of the rent receipts and the tenant shall obtain a rent receipt on payment of rent from the landlord and if the landlord fails to grant any receipt, the tenant remedy lies under section 27 of the Premises rent control Act for penalty for the landlord for failure to grant receipt. 

 7. In the present suit admittedly there is no such plea taken by the tenant that he made grievance to the house rent controller that the landlord willfully refused to grant him rent receipt though he paid rent for the month of December, 1996 and January, 1997 within the time allowed by the Premises. Rent Control Act. On a perusal of section 13 of the Premises Rent Control Act, I am of the view that as soon as the relationship of landlord, the tenants is established, the onus is on the tenant to prove payment of monthly rents and such proof must be established on the basis of rent receipts or by any paper showing payment of rent in writing signed by the landlord and no oral evidence is permissible or admissible to prove payment of monthly rents. In the present case, admittedly there is no rent receipts or any written receipts signed by the landlord accepting monthly rents for the month of December, 1996 and January, 1997. This aspect of the case was not legally considered by the trial court. The trial court failed to notice that the defendant have failed to prove payment of rent according to law and became a defaulter for non-payment of rent for the month of December, 1996 and January, 1997 and is not entitled to any protection from eviction. The learned S.C.C. Judge made a wrong approach to the pleadings of the parties and placed the onus wrongly on the landlord to prove non-payment of rent by the tenant. The learned S.C.C. Judge misconstrued the plaintiffs case and erred in law in holding that the defendant is in possession by holding over: In view of my aforesaid finding I am of the view that the defendants became defaulters in respect of the suit premises and they are not entitled to any protection from eviction. 

 judgment and decree dated 14.9.99 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Sadar Chittagong iii S.C.C. Suit No. 7 of 1997 is hereby set aside and the suit stands decreed. The defendants are directed to vacate the suit premises in favour of the plaintiff within 60 days from the date of the receipt of the records by the trial court failing which the plaintiff shall get possession of the suit premises in accordance with law. The plaintiffs are also entitled to recover the arrear rents as claimed in the plaint.
